subject: Control-plane / Data-path segregation and evidence package for Dedicated & Private
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security architecture + evidence request for Dedicated instance

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team asked for a written security architecture overview that clearly separates the control plane from the customer data path for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want:

- A diagram showing network flow for control-plane traffic (management, telemetry) vs customer data-plane (model inference, KV cache)
- Where keys live (KMS/HSM) and who has access to plaintext
- Egress/ingress controls, NAT, and peering model for VPC and on-prem
- Audit/logging locations for SOC 2 evidence and retention periods

Can you provide a brief document and any artifacts (diagram, SIG/CAIQ pointers, or SOC 2 evidence references) we can give to our InfoSec reviewer? Ideally by end of day Monday (US PST).

Jordan
Security Architect, Acme Corporation

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security architecture + evidence request for Dedicated instance

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear checklist. I pulled together a concise package and attached three artifacts: 1) high-level control-plane vs data-path diagram (redwood-controlplane-datapath-diagram-v3.png), 2) annotated SIG control-matrix that maps controls to our implementation and evidence (sig-control-matrix-annotated.xlsx), and 3) a short network segmentation checklist we use for Dedicated/Private installs (network-segmentation-checklist.pdf).

High-level notes:
- Control plane (managed by Redwood) is a separate set of services in our control VPC. Management traffic is TLS 1.3 mutual-auth, mTLS between control-plane services, and never transits customer VPCs.
- Data path for Dedicated sits entirely inside customer-managed subnet(s) when using Private (VPC/On-prem option) — compute nodes that serve inference reside in the customer tenant and are bound to the customer’s KMS for key encryption-at-rest. For Redwood Dedicated (hosted but dedicated pool), we provide dedicated GPU pools with network-level isolation and host-based hardening; customer data in transit is encrypted and we do not persist plaintext post-response unless explicitly configured.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS optional; for hosted Dedicated we support customer KMS via external key wrapping (Bring Your Own Key). Root keys are stored in FIPS 140-2 level HSMs (partner HSM). Only a limited Redwood KeyOps role can access key metadata; plaintext access is restricted and logged.
- Audit/logging: control plane emits operational logs to our control log cluster (retained 90 days by default; extended retention available). Data-plane access logs (request/response metadata) are written to the customer’s audit bucket for Private deployments and to a dedicated tenant for Dedicated with RBAC controls. All logs are forwarded to the SIEM in encrypted transit and we provide SOC 2 mappings for retention and access controls in the attached matrix.

If it helps, we can run a 30-45 minute walkthrough with your InfoSec team tomorrow. Grace — can you coordinate meeting times and capture any procurement/ticket links for the pack?

Thanks,
Soojin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-controlplane-datapath-diagram-v3.png (image/png), sig-control-matrix-annotated.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), network-segmentation-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Security architecture + evidence request for Dedicated instance

Team — forwarding Acme request and the artifacts I prepared. Need quick confirmation on two technical points before the walkthrough:

1) For Hosted Dedicated we call out that data-plane compute runs in logically isolated tenant pools. Markus — can you confirm the phrasing that we do not cross-tenant KV cache sharing and that eviction keys are per-tenant? If there are any extra notes around kernel isolation/secure compute please add.

2) For Private (VPC/on-prem) we say "keys reside in customer KMS where configured". Rishi — please confirm supported KMS types (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, on-prem HSM via PKCS#11) and whether we can state FIPS/HSM-backed with customer-managed keys in the customer naming. Also confirm network egress options (VPC peering, PrivateLink, customer-managed NAT gateway) we support for telemetry.

Grace — please pull HubSpot deal ACME-2026-0892 and include the procurement checklist link in the walkthrough invite; buyer will likely ask for SOC 2 report redacted copy and SIG completed answers for accounts in their procurement flow.

Thanks — trying to keep this to a short show-and-tell for InfoSec tomorrow.

— Soojin

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security architecture + evidence request for Dedicated instance

Soojin / Rishi — quick confirmations below for the deck:

- KV cache isolation: confirmed. Cache namespaces are tenant-bound; we never share in-memory KV across tenants. Eviction and rotation keys are tenant-scoped and rotated per our key rotation policy (30-90 days depending on control plane config).
- Kernel/Application isolation: Dedicated workloads run in hardened container runtimes with seccomp and apparmor profiles; for Private on-prem package we offer optional dedicated bare-metal with Sealing and TPM-based attestation for customers who require hardware-backed isolation.
- KMS support: Rishi will confirm list, but we support AWS KMS, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, and HSM via PKCS#11 adapters for on-prem.
- Telemetry egress: we support customer-controlled egress for Private deployments — telemetry can be routed over customer-managed VPN/ExpressRoute/Direct Connect, or pushed to a customer S3 blob in region. For Hosted Dedicated, telemetry is sent to our control plane over mTLS with IP allowlisting options and per-customer endpoints.

I'll add a short paragraph to the diagram legend clarifying "control-plane never injects customer data into control logs; data-plane request/response payloads are never retained by default" and call out SOC 2 mapping references in the matrix.

— Markus
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Jordan —

Thanks for the request and for the time yesterday. Per our materials and the follow-up review from our security team, attached is the evidence bundle that maps control areas to artifacts you requested. Highlights:

- redwood-controlplane-datapath-diagram-v3.png — annotated network diagram showing control-plane (management, orchestration, telemetry) boundaries and the customer-owned data path for Private/Dedicated installs. Legend includes ports, mTLS, and peering models.
- sig-control-matrix-annotated.xlsx — SIG control mapping and pointers to redacted SOC 2 evidence where applicable (log retention, RBAC reviews, key rotation logs).
- network-segmentation-checklist.pdf — checklist we use during Dedicated and Private rollouts; includes firewall rules, subnet allocation guidance, and NAT/eBPF notes.

Proposed next step: 30-minute walkthrough with our SecOps and Infra leads to run the diagram and answer any technical questions. Grace will send a calendar invite with the HubSpot procurement reference and a link to a redacted SOC 2 snapshot.

If you need specific exported logs or a Soc 2 report redaction, let us know via this thread and we’ll route the request through our compliance team.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
